card.name: Verbs after long historical subjects
card.fires_on: The word right after a long subject noun phrase in old-fashioned historical or biographical prose, usually where the main verb or auxiliary comes next (has, was, long, which, suffered).

modes.label: Auxiliary after subject
modes.description: A verb like has or was comes right after a long subject, before the rest of the predicate.
modes.example: The service rendered by the intellectual aristocracy of pioneer Massachusetts and the other New England colonies<< has>> long been accorded ample recognition.

modes.label: Word after abstract noun
modes.description: A word such as long, which or responsible follows a noun and starts a clause that describes it.
modes.example: Thus was conceived the idea<< responsible>> for the first publication of a scientific character

card.plain: It fires on the spot where the main verb or a describing clause begins after a long subject in old-style history writing.
